checked.label: 75 in 100 no longer hooked
problems: Arithmetic confirmed (Dawson 2005 abstract, re-fetched 2026-11-08 via Europe PMC): 25.0 dependent + 27.3 partial remission + 11.8 asymptomatic risk + 17.7 low-risk + 18.2 abstainers = 100.0. So 75.0 in 100 no longer met full dependence criteria in the past year. 11.8+17.7+18.2 = 47.7, so 'about 48 in 100 with no signs left' is right.

Is the headline more hopeful than the source? Slightly, yes. 27.3 of the 75 are 'partial remission': they still had dependence or abuse signs in the past year, and the source does not count them as recovered. The headline 'no longer were' reads as free, and only the caveat in the fold says otherwise. The r4 owner-lens even proposed 48 in 100 for this reason. Keep 75 (D7), but put the qualifier on the face, with no second figure.
Measured still uses % while the other rev4 cards turned shares into 'N in 100' (D7 'everywhere on reader faces'). Fixed to match.
Quote covers only 25.0 and 25.5. That is acceptable, since the other categories are in the same abstract sentence. A longer quote would go over 30 words.

fix.beliefs[2].test: Write down one hard week you got through, and what carried you. Still drinking? Drinking heavily every day? Read Before you stop first. If not, spend one evening you'd usually drink on a long walk, no drink. Already off it? Take that walk when the next pull comes. Rate the pull at the start and the end: 0 is none, 10 is can’t hold on.

fix.beliefs[3].test: Still drinking? Drinking heavily every day? Read Before you stop before any night without drink. Otherwise, on three nights this week note how long you took to fall asleep and how often you woke; set a night you drank against one you didn’t. Already off it? Note the same for three nights and set it against how you slept when you drank.

checked.label: footer amount + emergency line
problems: Re-fetched 2026-11-08. NHS: 'One unit equals 10ml or 8g of pure alcohol'; a pint at 3.6% is 2 units and at 5.2% is 3 units; 'A 750ml bottle of … wine (ABV 13.5%) contains 10 units'. NIAAA: a standard drink 'contains about 14 grams'. NICE CG115 1.3.4.1: 'over 15 units of alcohol per day'.

15 units = 120 g. Pints: 5 (at 5.2%) to 7.5 (at 3.6%), so '5 to 7' is fine. Wine: exactly 1.5 bottles at 13.5%. US drinks: 120/14 = 8.6, so 'about 8' is rounded down, not to the nearest whole number. Changed to '8 to 9 US drinks', which matches NIAAA and keeps the low end, the safer side.

'cut back sharply' in the emergency line is backed by the ASAM quote ('cessation of (or reduction in) alcohol use'). D10 met (US drinks and wine added). Rule 30 avoidance of 'a bottle and a half' noted.
The NICE quote note says 'about 6 to 7 pints of 4% beer' while the text says 5 to 7. Both are right (different strengths), no change.

fix.footerProposal.text: Drinking heavily every day (UK doctors draw the line at about 15 units a day: 8 to 9 US drinks, 5 to 7 pints of beer, or 1.5 bottles of wine), shaky, sweaty or sick in the morning until you drink, or had a seizure or the DTs before? Talk to a doctor before you stop or cut back sharply: seizures can come 8–48 hours later, and each withdrawal can be worse. A seizure, confusion, seeing or hearing things, or visible shaking after you stop or cut back sharply is an emergency: call an ambulance.
